stem: Solstice Payroll classifies its core DB as high criticality and defines a small blast radius goal for failures while balancing backup cost.

choices.text: Use one monthly manual snapshot only across production, staging, and test databases to simplify policy administration.
Use tighter restore-point intervals and isolate failures so unaffected components stay outside the impact scope.
Disable PITR to simplify retention governance and reduce restore options.
Use one shared development retention policy for every workload class.

rationale: Critical workloads with tight recovery goals need stronger backup cadence and fault isolation that limits affected scope. Monthly-only snapshots are too coarse for this requirement. Disabling PITR removes useful recovery flexibility. Applying one dev-oriented policy to all classes ignores business criticality differences.
